steps.title: Import Vue and lifecycle hooks
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the onMounted, onUpdated, and onUnmounted lifecycle hooks from 'vue'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and the specific lifecycle hooks you'll need for this lesson.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a module
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and the lifecycle hooks here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start working with Vue lifecycle hooks.
successCriteria: Vue, onMounted, onUpdated, and onUnmounted are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and the lifecycle hooks needed for this lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing all the required items: Vue, onMounted, onUpdated, and onUnmounted from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import Vue and the three lifecycle hooks from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'SideEffectDemo' using the script setup syntax.
steps.hint: Use the <script setup> tag to define a Vue component. You can start with an empty template for now.
steps.analogousExample: // Example of a Vue component with script setup
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic Vue component structure with script setup ready for adding side effect logic.
successCriteria: The component is named 'SideEffectDemo' and uses <script setup> syntax with a template section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Vue component structure. This gives us a foundation to add side effect logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the <script setup> syntax and have both script and template sections.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a Vue component with the correct structure. Remember to use <script setup> and include a template.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, declare a reactive state variable named 'count' using ref and initialize it with the value 0.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported from Vue to create a reactive reference. The syntax is: const count = ref(0);
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a reactive variable
const message = ref('Hello');
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive count variable is created with an initial value of 0, ready to be used in the template.
successCriteria: The code includes 'const count = ref(0);' inside the <script setup> section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a reactive state variable using ref. This count variable will automatically update the UI when its value changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the ref function correctly. Check that you've written 'const count = ref(0);' inside the <script setup> section.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to use the ref function from Vue to create a reactive variable. The syntax should be: const count = ref(0);

steps.title: Initialize reactive state for side effect tracking
steps.instruction: Initialize a reactive message variable using ref with an initial value of 'No side effect yet' inside the <script setup> section.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create a new reactive reference. Place it after your existing state declaration.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a reactive message
const message = ref('Initial message');
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reactive message variable ready to track side effect status.
successCriteria: A message variable is declared with ref and initialized to 'No side effect yet'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the reactive state needed to track side effects.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref() and setting the initial value to 'No side effect yet'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Initialize a message variable using ref with 'No side effect yet' as the initial value.

steps.title: Define a handler to update state
steps.instruction: Define a function named increment that increases the count value by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that modifies the reactive count variable using .value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named increment is defined that modifies the count reactive state.
successCriteria: The increment function is defined and increases count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the increment handler that updates the reactive state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You defined a function, but make sure it correctly increases count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment function is not defined correctly. Check that it modifies count.value.

steps.title: Use onMounted for initial side effect
steps.instruction: Import the onMounted lifecycle hook from 'vue' and use it to set the message state to 'Component mounted!' when the component first loads.
steps.hint: Import onMounted alongside ref, then call onMounted with a callback function that updates message.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The onMounted hook is imported and used to update the message state when the component mounts.
successCriteria: onMounted is imported from 'vue' and called with a function that sets message.value to 'Component mounted!'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used onMounted to run code when the component first loads.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported onMounted and called it with a function that updates message.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onMounted hook isn't set up correctly. Import it from 'vue' and use it to update message when the component mounts.

steps.title: Use onUpdated for reactive updates
steps.instruction: Import the onUpdated lifecycle hook from 'vue' and use it to update the message whenever the count changes.
steps.hint: You'll need to add onUpdated to your import statement and call it with a callback function that updates message.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The onUpdated hook will execute whenever reactive state changes, allowing you to perform side effects in response to updates.
successCriteria: onUpdated is imported from 'vue' and used with a callback that updates message.value based on count.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported and used onUpdated to track reactive state changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've both imported onUpdated and called it with a callback function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onUpdated hook isn't properly set up. Check that you've imported it and used it correctly.

steps.title: Use onUnmounted for cleanup
steps.instruction: Import the onUnmounted hook from 'vue' and use it to log a cleanup message when the component is destroyed.
steps.hint: Add onUnmounted to your existing import statement, then call onUnmounted with a function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The onUnmounted hook is imported and used to log a cleanup message when the component is destroyed.
successCriteria: onUnmounted is imported from 'vue' and called with a function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented cleanup logic with onUnmounted.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've both imported onUnmounted and called it with a function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported onUnmounted from 'vue' and used it to log a cleanup message.

steps.title: Create the template structure
steps.instruction: Inside the template, create a div container with a class of 'container' to wrap the component's content.
steps.hint: Add a div element with the class attribute set to 'container' inside the template section.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a div container with a class attribute, ready to hold the UI elements.
successCriteria: A div element with class="container" exists inside the template tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the container structure for your component's UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div with class="container" inside the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Add a div element with class="container" inside the template tags.

steps.title: Add UI elements and wire events
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a paragraph to display the current count value, a paragraph to display the message value, and a button that calls the increment function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display reactive values in the template. Add a @click directive to the button to call your increment function.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying reactive values and wiring events
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display the current count and message values, and clicking the button will increment the count.
successCriteria: Template contains a paragraph showing count value, a paragraph showing message value, and a button with @click="increment".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the UI elements and wired the button event. The component now displays state and responds to user interaction.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have both paragraphs displaying the count and message values, and that the button has the @click directive calling the increment function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required elements. Add a paragraph for count, a paragraph for message, and a button with @click="increment".
